About the Position:
The Combat Capabilities Development Command (DEVCOM) is the Army's technology leader. It ensures the dominance of the Army by creating, integrating, and delivering technology-enabled solutions. Whether providing solutions to meet current operations or developing break-through technologies for the next generation, DEVCOM is at the forefront of what the Soldier eats, wears, fires and drives.
Details.AgencyMarketingStatement: Civilian employees serve a vital role in supporting the Army mission. They provide the skills that are not readily available in the military, but crucial to support military operations. The Army integrates the talents and skills of its military and civilian members to form a Total Army. The Army values diversity of perspectives, backgrounds, cultures and skills, which connects employees to organizations that are committed to building an inclusive work environment where they can contribute to their fullest potential. Note: Management may make selections at any grade level. Promotion to the next grade will be at management's discretion following completion of time-in-grade requirements, training, fully successful performance, and acquired and demonstrated experience. This position has been identified as telework eligible. The determination of duration, amount, and frequency is at the discretion of management and as duties and mission dictate. Telework is not guaranteed - the eligibility can be revoked at any time due to lack of sufficient equipment for the incumbent to work effectively in a telework environment, change of duties and/or mission that now requires the incumbents physical presence, an incumbent violating the terms of the Telework Authorized Use Policy (AUP), or a decline or failure in incumbent's work performance.
MajorDuties: Incumbent is responsible for the planning, development, and execution of social media and web presence and engagement for DEVCOM.

Respond, in oral and written form, to requests for information by determining the nature of the information required and collecting and assembling the material using the appropriate format and style based on needs and organization practices.
Prepare content for authorized social media sites (such as Facebook, Flickr, Twitter, etc.) and organization's web page and posts content following approval process.
Manage the social media program by soliciting submissions, writing, editing brief news releases and photos related to appropriate events for organization personnel.
Develop written materials which transmit information concerning the nature and purpose of the organization?s programs, projects, items of concern to the general public or more specialized publics.
Take photographs, records and edits video, develops graphics and presents artwork for composition and selects the most newsworthy for inclusion in desired publications.
Plan and execute information campaigns in accordance with the command?s mission and vision.
Advise program officials regarding the content and presentation of information materials submitted for dissemination or other information purposes.
The incumbent will also advise internal staff how to properly engage in social media.
Coordinates with both internal and external stakeholders to develop effective digital communication strategies.

Details.AgencyMarketingStatement:
Civilian employees serve a vital role in supporting the Army mission. They provide the skills that are not readily available in the military, but crucial to support military operations. The Army integrates the talents and skills of its military and civilian members to form a Total Army. Fort Bliss supports over 30,000 troops, and has undergone the largest post expansion in the Army. It is the home of the 1st Armored Division, FORSCOM deployable units, and has a full scope of base support elements. It is home to the U.S. Army Sergeant's Major Academy, William Beaumont Army Hospital, 32nd Army Air and Missile Defense Command, Joint Modernization Command, and Joint Task Force North. Ft Bliss plays a vital role in America's largest city on a U.S. International Border, El Paso, Texas. El Paso's climate is dry/sunny with mild winters and warm summers.

Produce digital copies of recorded events.

Details.AgencyMarketingStatement: This position is located in the Defense Media Activity (DMA), a Department of Defense Field Activity reporting to the Assistant to the Secretary of Defense (Public Affairs) (ATSD (PA)). The DMA is a worldwide media organization charged with informing Department of Defense (DoD) audiences, managing the Department's visual information records, training the Department's public affairs and visual information workforce and providing broadcast radio and television to DoD personnel overseas operating from multiple locations in the United States and overseas, including deployed combat and contingency forces worldwide.
MajorDuties: As a Audiovisual Production Specialist at the GS-1071-11 some of your typical work assignments may include: Collaborates in planning sessions with clients, including the senior level military public affairs officials to coordinate best methods for capturing and transmitting an event for streaming on DoD Web platforms and for posting to the Defense Visual Information Distribution Service (DVIDS). Studies scripts and other program information, before broadcasting to define sets, camera angles, and lighting and to arrange the sequencing of graphics and other visual materials needed and directs live broadcasts. Directs and helps to identify the best distribution paths to stream and share video products on DoD Web platforms world-wide. Operates with expertise video cameras, editing equipment, including recorders, switchers, broadcast routers, computer software editors, character generators, audio mixers, microphones, and graphics generators to produce preliminary and final video products. Produces and creates live webcast or television broadcast of coverage-of-record for OASD (PA) of DoD public affairs briefings and events for worldwide dissemination and permanent archive.

You may qualify at the GS-11, if you fulfill the following qualifications: A. One year of specialized experience equivalent to the GS-09 grade level in the Federal service: Independently operating audio-visual broadcast quality equipment such as, video cameras, studio/field tripods, audio mixing boards, microphones, and lighting in a studio or field environment; OR B. I have successfully completed a Ph.D. or 3 full years of progressively higher level graduate education leading to such a degree or LL.M., if related. Information forums/avenues planned and managed include but are not limited to: production of audio visual presentations and broadcast materials; newspapers as well as news and feature items for publication; web sites; special events; and other methods. 2. Plans, organizes and administers an AFRC wing external information program. Establishes and maintains effective working relationship with print and broadcast media representatives in disseminating information or answering inquiries about the organizations' operations or activities.

Briefs those members on Air Force Reserve and local unit missions, budgets, economic impact, and personnel issues. Maintains documentation of all congressional contacts in the public affairs office and reports all activity to HQ AFRCIP AB.

The Army values diversity of perspectives, backgrounds, cultures and skills, which connects employees to organizations that are committed to building an inclusive work environment where they can contribute to their fullest potential. This position is located in Vicenza, Italy. The Vicenza Area is the home of the modularized and expanded 173d Airborne Brigade Combat Team and a deployable command post of Task Force 5. It is the ideal geographic location. Vicenza is a beautiful city steeped in rich history, with a wealth of cultural, recreational and entertainment opportunities.
